title: Kestrel and the Crown
premise: In the city of Vaelmoor, magic has been outlawed for a generation, and Lena Ashgrove survives by selling harmless charms while hiding a gift that could get her hanged. When the crown's new witch-hunters begin dragging gifted people into the palace and none return, Lena discovers the king himself is bound to an ancient entity wearing his crown — and that her own debt-contract was written to deliver her to it. Forced to ally with a disgraced hunter who knows the palace's secrets and a rebel archivist who holds the binding rites, Lena must choose between exposing the truth (which will destroy the loyal friend who serves the crown) or letting the entity complete its slow possession of the realm. In the end, Lena unbinds the king at the cost of her own gift, exposes the hunt as the entity's design, and leaves Vaelmoor free but forever changed.
about_author: J. M. Eastwick is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about ordinary people trapped in systems larger than themselves, from a cluttered study full of unlabeled keys.

chapters.title: The Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Lena Ashgrove, POV. Lena sells a luck charm to a dockworker and returns to the temple where she serves out her family's debt as a scribe. A routine audit reveals her contract has been quietly amended — a clause she never signed. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath daily routine.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. The crown proclaims the Great Purification: all gifted persons must register or be hunted. Lena watches a neighbor's shop burn and realizes her charms have been traced. She burns her own stock but keeps one charm she cannot explain. Beat: fear hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Hunter's Oath
chapters.summary: Corin Vale, POV. Introduce Corin, a witch-hunter who has begun doubting the hunt after interrogating a child who genuinely has no gift. His commander orders him to Vaelmoor's temple district. Beat: conscience cracking under duty.

chapters.title: What the Ink Remembers
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. Copying temple records, Lena finds five years of missing pages — every entry mentioning the king's coronation excised. The temple's high scribe warns her to stop asking. Beat: the thrill and terror of a hidden pattern.

chapters.title: A Knock at Midnight
chapters.summary: Corin, POV. Corin raids the temple and finds Lena mid-ritual, protecting a frightened apprentice. Instead of arresting her, he covers for them — an act of treason he can't justify even to himself. Beat: the first betrayal of his oath.

chapters.title: The Thing in the Throne Room
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. Summoned to the palace to 'register,' Lena senses the wrongness of the court: courtiers with glassy eyes, a king who repeats phrases like a recording. She glimpses the crown breathing. Beat: horror confirmed; stakes made personal.

chapters.title: Bargains in Borrowed Light
chapters.summary: Lena and Corin, alternating. Corin offers uneasy alliance: he'll get her into the archives if she proves the king is enchanted, not merely mad. Neither trusts the other. Beat: reluctant partnership forged in mutual blackmail.

chapters.title: The Archivist Below
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. In the sealed under-archive they meet Sable Ives, a rebel archivist living among banned books, who reveals the binding rite: the entity called the Regent has worn three kings already. Beat: hope with a price tag attached.

chapters.title: Five Years of Small Charms
chapters.summary: Lena, POV flashback chapter. Her childhood, her mother's arrest, the debt that bound her — and the revelation that the temple sold her contract to the crown deliberately, breeding a vessel for the Regent. Beat: grief reframing everything she thought she survived.

chapters.title: The Loyal Blade
chapters.summary: Corin, POV. Corin's closest friend, Captain Dree, grows suspicious of his absences. Torn between loyalty and truth, Corin feeds her a half-lie that will later cost him dearly. Beat: loyalty beginning to curdle.

chapters.title: Rite of Unbinding
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. The trio studies the unbinding: it requires a willing vessel's consent, a name spoken truly, and a life offered freely. The last requirement goes conveniently unexplained. Beat: dread dressed as instruction.

chapters.title: The Hunt Comes Home
chapters.summary: Corin, POV. The purge reaches the under-archive; Sable is captured covering their escape. Corin must watch, powerless, as his own machinery devours an ally. Beat: guilt and fury intertwined.

chapters.title: Audience with the Crown
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. Dragged before the king, Lena realizes the Regent knows exactly what she is — and offers her freedom in exchange for surrendering willingly. It shows her mother, alive, in a vision. Beat: temptation sharpened into a knife.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Corin, POV. Captain Dree confronts Corin with evidence of his treachery. He refuses to recant; she arrests him, weeping. Beat: the theme made flesh — loyalty vs. truth, and no clean side.

chapters.title: The Cell and the Key
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. Imprisoned beside Corin, Lena learns the amended clause in her contract makes her legally the Regent's property. The apprentice from Chapter 5 smuggles them Sable's stolen notes. Beat: despair punctured by small defiance.

chapters.title: The King Beneath
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. In a dream-walk forced by the Regent, Lena meets the real king, Aldric, buried alive inside his own mind. He begs her not to save him if the price is another vessel. Beat: compassion complicating the mission.

chapters.title: Breaking the Circle
chapters.summary: Corin and Lena, alternating. Escape through the palace's bone-choked foundations; Corin sacrifices his hunter's insignia — and his legal existence — to open the final gate. Beat: identity burned as fuel.

chapters.title: The Price Named Plainly
chapters.summary: Sable, POV, from captivity. Interrogated by the Regent itself, Sable learns the unbinding's true cost: the caster loses their gift permanently, and something more — the rite demands a memory of love as anchor. Sable passes this out through a sympathetic guard. Beat: knowledge arriving too late to be kind.

chapters.title: Crownfall
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. Climax. Before the assembled court, Lena speaks the king's true name and begins the unbinding as the Regent tears the room apart. Corin holds the line against Dree's soldiers without killing; Sable, freed in the chaos, anchors the rite. Beat: everything staked at once.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. The Regent is unbound; King Aldric wakes, aged and hollow, and abdicates rather than rule what he can't remember ruling. Lena's gift is gone — she feels its absence like a pulled tooth. Beat: victory with a wound in it.

chapters.title: Ledgers Closed
chapters.summary: Corin, POV. The hunt is dissolved; Dree, learning the truth, chooses loyalty to Corin over loyalty to the old order. Lena's debt contract burns publicly. Quiet reckonings, apologies that don't fix things but are made anyway. Beat: aftermath, tender and unsentimental.

chapters.title: Kestrel, Flying
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. Months later, Lena runs a bookshop with Sable, teaching children letters instead of charms. A kestrel lands on her windowsill — the shape her gift sometimes took — and she lets it go. Beat: peace earned, not given; survival's price finally named as worth paying.
